item.description:

You've got the guy with the "masculine energy" comments and giant wife statue, the multiple times divorcee that lies about be a pro gamer and has the political opinions of your uncle at Thanksgiving, etc. Un-cool.

item.title: Comment on The culture that is German (Roman) by SpeculativeDiction
item.description:
What seems crazy to me from outside Europe about European politics and the "rise of the far right" is how the entire thing seems to be about uncontrolled migration but few parties (particularly on the left) seem willing to move to the centre on this issue.

I understand and accept all the arguments for the good of immigration. I am an immigrant myself (admittedly from one Anglosphere nation to another so the cultural differences are minimal). But is it not possible for countries to decide they have had enough immigration for the timebeing and prefer a period of much lower immigration rates? It seems like whenever this is presented the argument about retiree ratios etc is rammed down your throat but is that all nations are? Carehomes for the elderly who must simultaneously maintain their home values, cradle to grave care, and a state willing to pay any and all expenses to give them one extra day?

It seems to me as soon as any moderate party adopts a sane position on immigration (e.g. a nations first responsibility is to its citizens, not all immigrants are equally beneficial to existing citizenry, there are times where immigration should be lower than current levels, and illegal immigrants are lawbreakers who should be deported) the energy in the "far right" will vanish completely. There will still be some ethnonationalist loons out there but most people aren't that, they just don't want anymore immigration for economic and cultural reasons (and the lifestyle impacts this can have).
